tasks.gr11-gas-exchange-t3: Topic: Gas Exchange. Cover the structure of the human breathing system (nasal cavity, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli), the mechanics of inhalation and exhalation (intercostal muscles, diaphragm, lung volume and pressure changes), gas exchange across the alveolar membrane by diffusion, features of alveoli that aid gas exchange (thin walls, moist surface, large surface area, rich blood supply), and homeostatic control of breathing rate by the medulla oblongata. Ask Grade 11 learners to describe ventilation steps, label breathing system diagrams, and explain alveolar adaptations.
tasks.gr11-excretion-humans-t3: Topic: Excretion in Humans. Cover the structure of the kidney (cortex, medulla, pelvis) and the nephron (Bowman's capsule, glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, collecting duct), the three processes of urine formation — ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption, and tubular secretion — composition of filtrate versus urine, kidney failure symptoms, and medical interventions such as dialysis and kidney transplant. Ask Grade 11 learners to sequence urine formation, label nephron diagrams, compare filtrate and urine composition, and evaluate dialysis as a treatment.
tasks.gr11-population-ecology-t3: Topic: Population Ecology. Cover population measurements (size, density, natality, mortality, immigration, emigration), S-shaped and J-shaped growth curves, carrying capacity, interspecific and intraspecific competition, predator–prey relationships, symbiosis (mutualism, commensalism, parasitism), and ecological succession (primary and secondary). Ask Grade 11 learners to interpret population growth graphs, calculate population changes, explain ecological interactions, and describe succession stages.
